Subject: Request: custom SLA exhibit & fallback integration checklist

Hi Sergio / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our platform team reviewed the standard MSA/SOW and have two areas they'd like to lock down before we route to legal:

1) Weekend maintenance carveout — we need explicit language that allows BrightCare one regularly scheduled maintenance window (Sunday 02:00–06:00 PT) that may be excluded from availability calculations, plus an escalation path if an unplanned outage intersects with that window.

2) Integration checklist & evidence — our auditors require:
  - a short ops runbook showing failover steps (region-to-region),
  - telemetry endpoints we can query for uptime/latency (or an agreed snapshot cadence), and
  - a template for evidence submission in case of a SLA credit claim.

I've attached a short question list (BrightCare_SLA_Questions.pdf) and highlighted the sections where they want alternate order form language (primarily the availability exhibit and order form references to uptime credits).

Can Redwood propose exhibit wording we can share with our legal/procurement? Also please indicate if Dedicated vs Hosted changes any of the wording (we plan to start on hosted). If we can get a consolidated proposal + a suggested DocuSign timeline, procurement will prioritize review.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if it's easier.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Sr. Procurement Manager | BrightCare Health Systems

Thanks for the ping. Quick technical redlines and operational constraints below — please fold into the exhibit draft.

1) Baseline SLOs: For hosted we typically guarantee 99.9% monthly availability at the API layer. 99.95% is achievable but requires Dedicated or a documented multi-region routing setup with active failover (and will change unit economics). Recommend offering 99.9% hosted / 99.95% Dedicated as options in the order form.

2) Maintenance carveout language (suggested clause):
"Scheduled maintenance windows, not to exceed 4 hours per week and 8 hours per calendar month, may be excluded from Availability calculations if Redwood provides (i) advance notice of 72 hours, and (ii) a post-maintenance report. Unplanned maintenance shall be treated as an outage for Availability calculations unless mutually agreed otherwise in writing."

3) Evidence & telemetry: we can provide a weekly snapshot (ISO-8601 timestamped) of the availability metrics and an evidence template for credit claims. We do not, for security reasons, give unrestricted read access to internal telemetry endpoints; instead we provide export snapshots or a read-only metrics feed via a secured API key with limited retention (90 days).

4) Failover/runbook: Ops can produce a two-page runbook excerpt showing detection, failover trigger thresholds, and rollback steps. Want to confirm BrightCare's primary and secondary regions so we can simulate latency expectations.

5) Attachments: I'm attaching an evidence-runbook-template.pdf (stub) and suggest we add a short paragraph in the order form outlining the acceptance and DocuSign timeline (we typically need 7 business days after legal sign-off to schedule a Dedicated provisioning; hosted changes can be effective on the signature date).

If you want, I can draft a short redline of the order form paragraph that maps to the exhibit.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference

Elena — attaching our consolidated proposal based on procurement feedback and ops redlines. Highlights:

- Two SLO options included in the order form: Hosted = 99.9% monthly / Dedicated = 99.95% monthly.
- Scheduled maintenance carveout: allowed as you requested (Sunday 02:00–06:00 PT) with 72-hour notice and quarterly calendar obligation. Clause provided in exhibit.
- Evidence & runbook: we will provide a two-page runbook excerpt, a weekly availability snapshot export (retained 90 days), and an evidence-template for credit claims. We will not expose raw internal metrics endpoints; instead we deliver secured exports or a read-only metrics feed with scoped keys.
